# USB Serial Debugging
This firmware implements debugging output via USART2, which can be accessed through a USB-to-Serial adapter or ST-Link's virtual COM port.
## Hardware Setup
The STM32L432KC USART2 pins are connected as follows: - **TX (PA2)**: Transmit data from MCU to PC - **RX (PA3)**: Receive data from PC to MCU - **Baudrate**: 115200 bps, 8N1
## Connection Options
### Option 1: ST-Link V2/V3 Virtual COM Port If your ST-Link debugger supports virtual COM port: 1. Connect your ST-Link to the board 2. The USART2 pins are typically routed to the ST-Link 3. Find the virtual COM port on your system (e.g., `/dev/ttyACM0` on Linux)
### Option 2: External USB-to-Serial Adapter (FTDI, CP2102, etc.) 1. Connect adapter GND to board GND 2. Connect adapter RX to board PA2 (TX) 3. Connect adapter TX to board PA3 (RX) 4. Find the COM port (e.g., `/dev/ttyUSB0` on Linux)
## Viewing Debug Output
### Linux/macOS ```bash # Using screen screen /dev/ttyACM0 115200
# Using minicom minicom -D /dev/ttyACM0 -b 115200
# Using cat (read-only) cat /dev/ttyACM0 ```
### Windows Use PuTTY, TeraTerm, or Arduino Serial Monitor: - Port: COM3 (or check Device Manager) - Baudrate: 115200 - Data bits: 8 - Parity: None - Stop bits: 1
## Usage in Code
Use the `usb_println!` macro anywhere in your code:
```rust usb_println!("Hello from UWB Anchor!"); usb_println!("Counter value: {}", counter); usb_println!("Battery voltage: {} mV", voltage); ```
The macro supports the same formatting as `println!` and automatically adds line endings.
## Example Output
``` UWB Anchor Initialized System ready for debugging via USB Heartbeat: 0 Heartbeat: 1 Heartbeat: 2 ... ```
## Implementation Details
- Uses Embassy async USART driver with DMA for efficient transfers - 16-message buffered channel for non-blocking sends - Messages up to 256 bytes supported - Automatic CRLF line endings for terminal compatibility
